analysis.one_liner: Adani Ports & SEZ builds and operates a network of ports, terminals, logistics parks and a Special Economic Zone across India and select overseas sites (Colombo, Haifa, Tanzania and others), earning fees from cargo and container handling.
analysis.whats_happening: The board meets on 28 October 2026 (within a week) to approve Q2/H1 FY27 results. Ahead of that, operational data already shows H1 FY27 cargo volumes up 15% YoY to 280 MMT, with September alone up 11% YoY to 46 MMT. The company has also been expanding: it incorporated Paradip Mahanadi Terminal Ltd on 6 October 2026 (18 MMT dry-bulk capacity, 30-year concession, taking total handling capacity to 671 MMT), and on 30 September 2026 announced a $750 million plan to double Colombo West International Terminal's capacity to 3.2 million TEU.
analysis.plain_terms: This is an infrastructure/logistics business - it earns money by moving cargo through the ports and terminals it owns, so revenue broadly tracks trade volumes plus whatever new capacity it adds. The tension: a large share of recent growth is coming from newer international and marine businesses (up 80% and 67% respectively last quarter) rather than the mature domestic ports portfolio, which management itself called 'steady'. The stock is priced at a premium (P/E near 31x), which assumes these newer, faster-growing pieces keep delivering - not a one-quarter event.
analysis.quarters: Q1 FY27 (June 2026 quarter): core revenue was reported around ₹10,821 crore (+19% YoY) by some sources and total income at ₹11,673.71 crore (+23.9% YoY) by others - these are not the same line item, so treat them as not strictly comparable. EBITDA was ₹6,541 crore (+19% YoY), implying a margin near 60%. Net profit (PAT) rose a slower 10.2% YoY to ₹3,649.5 crore - growth lagging revenue/EBITDA growth is worth watching, since it suggests depreciation, interest or tax are rising faster than operating income. Management attributed growth to international ports (+80%) and marine (+67%), calling domestic ports performance 'steady'. Q2 FY27 numbers land 28 October 2026.
analysis.performance_read: Returns have been strong and broad-based: +19.86% over 1 year versus Nifty -12.28% and peer JSWINFRA +7.6%; +127.84% over 3 years versus Nifty +17.78% and peer +93.53%; +133.89% over 5 years versus Nifty +25.37% and peer +105.9%. The stock is currently 7.9% below its 2 July 2026 peak of ₹1,883.2, within a 52-week range of ₹1,298.13-₹1,883.2. The only corporate action on record is an old 5:1 split in September 2010 - there has been no demerger or spin-off since, so this drawdown is ordinary volatility, not something that needs price-series adjustment.
analysis.valuation_read: Trailing P/E is around 31x and P/B around 4.2x, against ROE of ~16% and ROCE of ~12.45%. Why it looks expensive: the market is paying up for a pipeline of new capacity (Paradip, Colombo, and others) and for the faster-growing international/marine segments, not for the mature domestic ports book alone. Whether it is actually cheap depends on whether that pipeline converts into profit growth that catches up with revenue growth - on current numbers (PAT growth trailing EBITDA growth), that hasn't fully happened yet, so the valuation is a bet on execution rather than a statistically cheap entry point.
analysis.growth_read: Growth is a mix: cargo volumes are genuinely rising (+15% YoY in H1 FY27, broad-based across months), which is volume-led. But within that, the fastest growth is concentrated in international ports and marine operations (+80% and +67% in Q1 FY27) while the core domestic ports business is merely 'steady' - so an increasing share of blended growth is coming from newer, smaller-base segments rather than uniform expansion across the whole network.
analysis.health_read: EBITDA margins near 60% in the latest quarter suggest healthy operating cash generation typical of a ports business. Debt/Equity is moderate at ~0.66, which is manageable but not low for a company simultaneously funding several large projects (Paradip, a $750 million Colombo expansion, and others). One source referenced an S&P rating upgrade around the Q1 FY27 results, but this is from a single outlet and not independently cross-checked - treat with caution. The bigger watch item here is execution/business risk - can it ramp up all these new assets as planned - rather than acute balance-sheet stress.
analysis.ownership_read: Promoter holding is reported around 66% as of mid-October 2026 (figures vary slightly, 66.0%-68.0%, depending on the reporting date), with the S.B. Adani Family Trust itself holding about 30.85% and the rest spread across several promoter entities (Carmichael Rail and Port Singapore, Adani Tradeline, Emerging Market Investment DMCC, Flourishing Trade and Investment). The promoter group has formally declared NIL encumbrance/pledge on these shares for FY26 - a clear improvement from 2020-21, when tens of millions of pledged shares were periodically released. FIIs hold roughly 16% and DIIs roughly 8%. Not verified: whether GQG Partners or any other marquee investor that bought into other Adani group companies post-2023 also holds a stake in Adani Ports specifically - check the latest NSE/BSE shareholding filing directly.
strengths: H1 FY27 cargo volumes up 15% YoY to 280 MMT, with September alone up 11% YoY to 46 MMT - genuine volume growth, not just pricing.
International ports (+80%) and marine (+67%) revenue growth in Q1 FY27 is diversifying the business beyond domestic ports.
EBITDA margin near 60% (₹6,541 crore EBITDA on ~₹10,821 crore revenue in Q1 FY27) reflects strong operating leverage.
Active capacity pipeline - Paradip Mahanadi Terminal (+18 MMT, 30-year concession, taking total capacity to 671 MMT) and the $750 million Colombo West expansion - extends the growth runway.
watchpoints: PAT growth of 10.2% YoY in Q1 FY27 lagged revenue/EBITDA growth of ~19-24% - the gap needs explaining via the Q2 FY27 results on 28 October 2026.
Valuation is rich at ~31x trailing earnings and ~4.2x book against a 16% ROE, leaving little room for a stumble in any of the ongoing expansion projects.
Multiple large, simultaneous capex commitments (Paradip, $750 million Colombo investment, and others) add funding and execution risk even though Debt/Equity (~0.66) looks moderate today.
Dividend yield is only 0.43%, so shareholder return depends almost entirely on continued earnings growth and price appreciation rather than income.
analysis.one_thing: The 28 October 2026 Q2/H1 FY27 results - specifically whether PAT growth closes the gap with the ~19-24% revenue/EBITDA growth rate, and whether the international-ports/marine momentum that drove H1 FY27 continues - will show whether the current premium valuation is earning its keep.
analysis.data_notes: Returns, peak/drawdown, 52-week range, dividend history and split data were taken directly from the verified data block and not recomputed. Q1 FY27 PAT (~₹3,649-3,650 crore) was cross-checked across multiple outlets (Angel One, The Statesman, Sahi, ScanX) and is consistent; the revenue figure differs between sources (₹10,821 crore 'revenue' vs ₹11,673.71 crore 'total income') and is flagged as not strictly comparable rather than averaged. Promoter shareholding percentage varies slightly (66.0%-68.0%) by reporting date; the most recent (16 October 2026) figure was used. The NIL-pledge declaration for FY26 was corroborated by a dedicated report. Could not verify any specific marquee institutional holder on the register or independently confirm the S&P rating-upgrade claim - both noted as unverified rather than stated as fact.
